statement: Monitor and Control Inventory Positions governed-by Develop Finished Product Inventory Policy
source_definition: Covers the recurring review of physical and book inventory positions, movements, and commitments; minimum, maximum, safety-stock, and operating-limit exceptions; short-term availability and imbalance risks; escalation and coordination of corrective actions; and maintenance of the operational inventory-position view that planning and execution consume — a recurring operational control rhythm that complements planning cycles. Excludes inventory-policy design (CM-1-1-3-7-1/-2/-3), formal measurement methodology (CM-1-1-3-7-4), reconciliation and adjustment governance (CM-1-1-3-7-5), and replenishment planning (CM-1-1-3-7-9); excludes the specialized consignment, commingled, re-brand, lot/batch, and third-party-storage arrangements (CM-1-1-3-7-6/-7/-8/-10/-11), except where those arrangements create an operational position exception requiring response; excludes day-to-day crude and feedstock position management, owned by Manage Feedstock Inventory (CM-1-2-5-4-2). target_definition: Covers policy for saleable products at refinery rack, terminal, and depot level, including service-level-driven safety stocks, seasonal and regulatory grade-transition stock rules, and segregation of branded versus unbranded stock. Sets the policy that Plan Finished Goods Inventory (CM-1-1-2-13) plans within — the plan-period target decision itself is owned there per its approved boundary. Excludes replenishment management, owned by Manage Inventory Replenishment (CM-1-1-3-7-9); excludes physical terminal operation, owned by Midstream. statement: Obtain Trade Approval governed-by Market Risk Management
source_definition: Covers the pre-execution authorization step: checking the deal against the trader's delegated authority, routing above-authority and non-standard deals (including structured deals) for escalated approval, and recording who approved what. Includes escalation and documented approval, rejection, or conditional approval of trades that exceed delegated authority, approach or breach a limit, are non-standard, or require a documented risk or compliance exception; it does not itself set, waive, or permanently amend risk limits, credit limits, or delegation-of-authority policy. The delegation of authority is set and maintained by Market Risk Management (Establish & Maintain Delegation Of Authority, CM-1-2-2-3-2); this process applies it. Excludes strategy approval, owned by Trading Strategy Management (CM-1-2-1-4); excludes post-trade compliance monitoring (Regulatory & Compliance, CM-1-2-4-3). An independent control function per the approved L3 definition; the delivery model is not prescribed. Excludes enterprise-wide strategic commodity-price risk, corporate hedging policy, capital allocation, and non-trading operating exposure unless those exposures are expressly booked into the governed trading portfolio. Excludes trading decisions and strategy stewardship, which are governed by these controls (CM-1-2-1-4); excludes credit risk (CM-1-2-2-1); excludes regulatory trading compliance (CM-1-2-4-3); excludes accounting P&L and its reconciliation ownership (Accounting, CM-1-2-4-2, with the economic-to-accounting reconciliation at CM-1-2-4-2-6); excludes independent model validation (designated validation function). statement: Negotiate Rebate governed-by Pricing Strategy Management
source_definition: Negotiation operates only within: the approved rebate architecture; approved customer/channel eligibility; delegated commercial authority; Legal/Compliance guardrails; pricing corridors and exception criteria; and contract and master-data controls. No individual arrangement may create a rebate structure, treatment, eligibility rule, payment term, customer classification, or price effect outside the approved architecture and delegation. Terms outside approved structures or thresholds require approval through Pricing Strategy Management governance and the applicable delegations before any commitment. Fact-dependent statement: where a rebate, discount, promotional allowance, or service/payment arrangement differs among purchasers that may compete, US price-discrimination or promotional-allowance requirements may be implicated depending on commodity comparability, purchaser status, competitive effect, available defenses, and other facts. Legal/Compliance determines applicability and sufficiency. Contractual formalization of agreed terms executes through the contract-management processes, not within this process. In scope: Prepare negotiation positions from approved structures and verified customer data | negotiate terms within architecture, eligibility, and delegation | secure required approvals | document agreed terms for implementation Out of scope: Creating rebate structures, treatments, eligibility rules, payment terms, customer classifications, or price effects outside the approved architecture | contract execution (Manage Contract & Order; Establish Commercial Terms & Contracts) | legal determinations (Legal/Compliance) | settlement
target_definition: Covers the pricing-strategy lifecycle: defining the strategic pricing approach (CM-1-3-3-2-1), developing the integrated pricing strategy (CM-1-3-3-2-2), defining the pricing measurement framework (CM-1-3-3-2-5), conducting pricing pilots (CM-1-3-3-2-4), and analyzing pricing performance (CM-1-3-3-2-3), with pilots and performance analysis operating as a feedback loop into the integrated strategy rather than a rigid sequence. The receiving side of the batch 22 price-role boundary. Develops and maintains approved price architecture, pricing rules, differential logic, index-linkage principles, discount/terms guardrails, and exception criteria under the applicable commercial, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and delegation-of-authority approvals. Approved parameters include price corridors, floors, and ceilings where governed, price-index and timing conventions where applicable, and discount/rebate guardrails — never rebate administration, specific posted prices, or contract rates. Execution stays out: transaction and sales pricing at CM-1-3-6-3; quote and contract pricing at CM-1-3-7-2. Where applicable, pricing strategy must be designed and applied with regard to price-discrimination risk in sales to competing purchasers, applicable defenses, contract structures, product comparability, competitive effects, state motor-fuel below-cost/unfair-sales laws, and other jurisdictional requirements. Legal and Compliance determine applicability and legal sufficiency. No pricing strategy, pilot, or performance analysis may use non-public competitor price, cost, capacity, customer, or future commercial information obtained through improper channels. Public, licensed, independently gathered, and legally permissible observations must be traceable to source and permitted use. Excludes transaction/sales pricing execution (CM-1-3-6-3); quote/contract pricing (CM-1-3-7-2); trading and supply pricing (CM-1-2, its processes); rebate design administration (CM-1-3-6-4); legal ownership of pricing law compliance (Legal, compliance framework); enterprise KPI definition (KPI workstream). In scope: Run the pricing-strategy lifecycle | develop and maintain approved price architecture, rules, parameters, and guardrails under the applicable approvals | pilot and analyze pricing as a feedback loop | operate within price-related legal frameworks | issue governed pricing direction to execution Out of scope: Transaction/sales pricing (CM-1-3-6-3) | quote/contract pricing (CM-1-3-7-2) | trading/supply pricing (CM-1-2) | rebate administration (CM-1-3-6-4) | pricing-law ownership (Legal, compliance) | enterprise KPI definition (KPI workstream) | specific posted prices and contract rates (execution)

statement: Manage Brand Standards and Inspections governed-by Manage Licensing & IP
source_definition: Standards change through governed change control, with Legal/IP review where standards touch protected marks. Inspection access, scope, records access, site-entry rules, and corrective-action requirements must follow the applicable agreement, operating authority, security rules, and safety requirements. Inspections produce findings and corrective-action coordination; remedies under franchise, dealer, and license agreements route through the relationship processes. Fact-dependent statement: where a remedy would affect a franchise relationship governed by the Petroleum Marketing Practices Act, the determination is reserved to Legal. Inspection evidence feeds Report Franchise Performance. Licensed-brand providers' own inspections of their standards are the provider's right under the license agreements; this process coordinates and consumes their outcomes. Where standards conflict or appear ambiguous, the process escalates interpretation to the licensor and Legal; it does not certify provider-standard compliance or modify provider standards. In scope: Standards definition, maintenance, publication, and change control | inspection planning and conduct where authorized | findings documentation | corrective-action plans agreed and tracked with relationship owners | escalation of unresolved or material issues | conformance reporting Out of scope: Statutory or legal notices, material-breach determinations, termination or nonrenewal, financial penalties, and litigation/arbitration (relationship management; Legal) | overriding operating or EHS authority | provider standards certification | imaging execution (CM-1-3-6-7-2) | training delivery (CM-1-3-6-1-4)
target_definition: Covers six concurrent functions: the intellectual-asset framework (CM-1-3-4-4-1), registration coordination (CM-1-3-4-4-2), valuation for decisions (CM-1-3-4-4-3), operational protection (CM-1-3-4-4-4), commercial exploitation (CM-1-3-4-4-5), and portfolio stewardship (CM-1-3-4-4-6). Operating-model note: This capability is cross-functional. Legal & Corporate Communications owns legal IP policy, filings, prosecution, enforcement, agreement drafting, execution, and legal advice. Commercial, Marketing, Product, R&D, and Innovation functions own business opportunity identification, commercial valuation evidence, use cases, licensing-business input, brand alignment, and portfolio recommendations within delegated authority. The taxonomy location does not prescribe a single organizational owner. Business-side asset identification, business input, commercial valuation, operational protection, exploitation opportunity identification, and portfolio stewardship are in scope. Legal work—filings, prosecution, maintenance filings, enforcement, litigation, drafting, review, and execution of IP/confidentiality/license agreements—belongs to Legal. Business recommendations and delegated commercial choices do not constitute legal determinations regarding registrability, patentability, freedom to operate, ownership, inventorship, infringement, validity, enforceability, confidentiality obligations, or territorial protection strategy. Those matters are determined by Legal and its authorized IP counsel. Intellectual assets span patents, trademarks (central to the branded-marketer and brand-licensing model, batches 21/22), trade secrets and know-how, copyrights, and data assets where classified as intellectual assets. Licensing economics operate within the pricing and commercial approval frameworks (batch 23); brand licensing aligns with Brand Strategy (CM-1-3-2-1) and, where franchise arrangements are affected, the batch 22 fact-dependent PMPA statement. Excludes IP legal work of every kind (Legal, locked rule); accounting valuation and impairment (Finance lock); brand strategy (CM-1-3-2-1); development of the underlying products (CM-1-3-4-3); R&D portfolio management (CM-1-3-4-5). In scope: Maintain the intellectual-asset framework | coordinate registration through Legal | value assets for business decisions | protect assets operationally | exploit assets commercially under delegated authority | steward the asset portfolio Out of scope: IP legal work and legal determinations (Legal, locked rule) | accounting valuation/impairment (Finance) | brand strategy (CM-1-3-2-1) | product development (CM-1-3-4-3) | R&D portfolio (CM-1-3-4-5)

statement: Define Financing & Payment Methods governed-by Maintain Credit Policies
source_definition: Methods considered where applicable include invoice/bank transfer, ACH/direct debit, card, fleet/fuel-card billing, prepayment, deposit, credit terms, financing programs, electronic payment, cash where relevant, currency and cross-border constraints where applicable, and surcharges, discounts, fees, incentives, or payment-method conditions subject to law and policy. statement: Perform Self-Billing Accounting governed-by Establish Commercial Terms & Contracts
source_definition: Self-billing operates only under executed agreements that meet the applicable tax-law conditions — fact-dependent by jurisdiction, determined by the Tax function; no self-billing without a qualifying agreement.
